transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been having a really hard time listening to people when they are talking directly to me. It constantly feels like my mind just drifts off, and people are getting frustrated with me because they think I'm ignoring them.
How long have you been having trouble paying attention and drifting off like this, and did it start in childhood or only more recently?

I've been struggling with this really badly for about a year now. But looking back, I've actually had these attention issues since I was a kid, definitely before I turned 12. It just seems to be impacting my life a lot more lately.
Over the past year, have you also been feeling down or losing interest or pleasure in things most days?
No, I haven't really felt down or lost interest in the things I enjoy. My struggles are definitely more about my trouble focusing and this constant sense of restlessness.
Do you also often feel physically restless, fidgety, or like you have to keep moving, or do you mainly have trouble with attention and forgetfulness?

I actually struggle with both types of difficulties. On the restless side, I have a hard time staying in my seat, tend to talk excessively, and often blurt out answers before people even finish asking. At the same time, I really struggle to listen when spoken to directly and constantly fail to follow through on instructions or finish tasks.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation), Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)], but the patient now reports clear hyperactive/impulsive symptoms in addition to inattention: difficulty staying seated, excessive talking, and blurting out answers. That makes predominantly inattentive presentation unlikely, leaving combined presentation as the best fit. The childhood onset and chronic attentional impairment support ADHD overall.

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms began in childhood before age 12 and are causing current impairment. The patient endorses both prominent inattentive symptoms (difficulty listening, drifting off, failing to follow through) and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (restlessness, difficulty staying seated, excessive talking, blurting out answers), which best fits the combined presentation. No evidence of depressed mood, anhedonia, mania, or psychosis was reported.
